principles.name: Bird in Hand
principles.definition: Begin with your identity, knowledge, abilities and relationships; let possible ends develop from these means.

principles.name: Affordable Loss
principles.definition: Bound commitments by what you can bear losing, rather than relying on predicted returns.

principles.name: Crazy Quilt
principles.definition: Build with self-selecting partners who commit resources and help shape the venture’s direction.

principles.name: Lemonade
principles.definition: Treat unexpected events as possible resources for new opportunities.

principles.name: Pilot in the Plane
principles.definition: Shape possibilities through actions and decisions within your influence, together with committed collaborators.

distinctions: Affordable loss neither guarantees profit nor authorises passing unpaid costs onto workers; each participant has different limits.
A conversation or contact is not yet a committed partnership. Commitments can change both resources and aims.
Agency concerns controllable choices, not control over audiences, markets or the entire future.
These are interacting principles, not five chronological project phases.
Applying them to cinema here is an editorial proposal, not evidence that historical filmmakers consciously followed the theory.
proposed_passage: Saras Sarasvathy’s five principles of effectuation offer another way to think about making something together.[^effectuation] Imagine a writer and director beginning with a story they have permission to adapt, skills they already possess and people willing to work with them: Bird in Hand. Affordable Loss asks what each can responsibly risk in developing it, without treating unpaid labour as somebody else’s contribution. Crazy Quilt takes the relationship further: a producer might commit development money, a theatre group rehearsal space, or a film society a licensed screening. Those commitments can help shape what becomes possible. Lemonade leaves room for an unexpected response—a conversation with viewers might reveal an audience or a form the makers had not considered. Pilot in the Plane brings the emphasis back to choices they can make together: the agreement, the work and the encounter with an audience. None promises a hit. It offers a way to begin, learn and share responsibility without waiting to predict the whole future.
proposed_note: [^effectuation]: UVA Darden, [Effectuation](https://www.darden.virginia.edu/effectuation); Effectuation.org, [The Five Principles of Effectuation](https://effectuation.org/the-five-principles-of-effectuation). Cinema examples are possibilities proposed here.
integration_advice: Use one compact passage within co-creation discussion. Do not repeat definitions as a second five-item checklist, impose deadlines, or turn the ending into a business-method lesson. Keep the human and literary question leading.
